ANSWER: The function that decides whether text looks like a secret is **`secret_kind`** in `src/memory/guard.rs` (line 53). It first checks the text against a set of named regex patterns (private keys, AWS keys, GitHub tokens, JWTs, etc.). If none match, it scans for any long token (32+ chars of `[A-Za-z0-9+/_=-]`) using the `LONG_TOKEN` regex, then calls the helper **`looks_random`** (line 62, same file) on each match. `looks_random` distinguishes high-entropy base64 keys from hex hashes and IDs by requiring the token to contain mixed-case letters *and* digits, then computing Shannon entropy and returning `true` only if entropy exceeds 4.2 bits per character—a threshold hex and base32 strings cannot reach.

CONFIDENCE: high
